idea-plugin.name: Multiple Run
idea-plugin.description:
Fork of the Multirun plugin by Ruslan Khmeliuk, with additional features such as an environment variables override applied to all grouped configurations. It replaces the original plugin (uninstall Multirun before installing this one).

Run multiple run configurations at once: group multiple run configurations and start them in a single click. Not only application and test run configurations can be grouped, but other Multiple Run configurations can be organized into single run configuration.

Use cases:

  • Start batch of tests for multiple modules or applications
  • Start multiple applications, like multiple servers or backend + web application

Usage:

  1. Run -> Edit Configurations...
  2. Find and add a new Multiple Run configuration
  3. Add other run configurations to the Multiple Run configuration
  4. Pick options you'd like
  5. Ready to use

Multiple Run + Before Launch Tasks gives even more functionality: read more at https://goo.gl/KwHvx

If this plugin saves you time, consider buying me a coffee ☕
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.0.15:

  • The Multiple Run Monitor now shows the new "Lanes" empty-state illustration instead of a plain "No run configurations are running" line when nothing is being monitored yet.

2.0.14:

  • Fix: running a group where a child configuration needed "Edit Configuration" first (an invalid/incomplete configuration, or one with "Edit configuration before run" checked) could throw a threading exception ("Access is allowed from Event Dispatch Thread only") and abort the run, instead of showing the edit dialog. The one-by-one delay/wait chaining runs this check from a background thread on purpose (so the wait doesn't freeze the IDE), but showing the dialog itself needs the UI thread - now correctly switches to it just for that part.

2.0.13:

  • Fix: creating a new Multiple Run configuration (or applying/running one) could throw a NullPointerException and leave the editor unusable. The 2.0.8 Kotlin migration declared the editor's resetEditorFrom/applyEditorTo parameter as non-null, but the platform can still call them with a null configuration while a brand-new entry is settling - the original Java implementation took a @Nullable parameter for exactly that reason and is now restored (with an explicit null check instead of relying on the type system).
  • Fix: the Multiple Run configuration type icon (and every other spot that reused it) rendered at 2.5x its intended size - it was accidentally sharing the plugin icon file, which must declare a 40x40 size for the Settings > Plugins list. Now uses a dedicated 16x16 icon with the same artwork.

2.0.12:

  • New visual identity: the "Lanes" mark (parallel process lanes + live status dots) replaces the generic platform icon everywhere the plugin shows its own branding - the plugin icon, the Multiple Run configuration type icon, and the Multiple Run Monitor tool window icon.
  • Custom icons for the actions that already had a generic platform icon: Refresh, Restart / Restart All, Stop / Stop Multiple Run, Show Columns, Switch Environment, Memory Analysis, the docker-compose import button, and the Processes/Logs tabs of the monitor tool window.
  • Docs: new logo at the top of the README and the wiki home page; a brand/BRAND_GUIDELINES.md design system doc (colors, iconography, voice) for anyone contributing UI.
  • No functional change - actions, shortcuts and behavior are unchanged, only their icons.

2.0.11:

  • Internal: finished renaming the fork's own internal identifiers from "Multirun" to "Multiplerun" - class/file names, log messages and comments now say "Multiplerun" (code) / "Multiple Run" (user-facing text) consistently.
  • Breaking for run configurations saved before this release: the run configuration type id itself changed from "Multirun" to "Multiplerun", so it can never collide with the original third-party Multirun plugin's own type id if both are ever installed together. This plugin has no real users yet, so the trade-off (existing saved configurations need to be recreated) was made now, while it is still free.
  • Docs: updated the README and Marketplace description to say "Multiple Run" instead of "Multirun" wherever they refer to this plugin - the historical credit line to the original Multirun plugin by Ruslan Khmeliuk is unchanged.

2.0.10:

  • Docs: revamped the README (feature sections now scannable at a glance, a screenshot up top) and added a support link for anyone who wants to buy the maintainer a coffee. No functional change.

2.0.9:

  • Internal (Kotlin migration, the rest of the codebase): converted the remaining 14 JUnit test classes from Java to Kotlin. Moved MultiplerunRunConfigurationEditor.form next to its Kotlin class under src/main/kotlin (confirmed the GUI-Designer form instrumentation still works from there). The entire codebase - src/main and src/test - is now Kotlin; there is no Java source left in the project. 145 tests still pass. No functional change.

2.0.8:

  • Internal (Kotlin migration complete): converted the last remaining Java class, MultiplerunRunConfigurationEditor (the run configuration editor UI), to Kotlin. It still binds to its existing GUI-Designer .form file - the form-to-bytecode weaving works the same for a Kotlin class as it did for Java, so the editor's layout and behavior are unchanged. src/main/java now contains no source files at all (100% Kotlin); only the test suite stays Java. No functional change.

2.0.7:

  • Internal (Kotlin migration, five classes - the last batch before the GUI-form-bound editor): converted MultiplerunRunner (the launcher extending GenericProgramRunner), AggregatedLogPanel (the docker-compose- logs-style aggregated Logs tab), MultiplerunRunnerState (the launch pipeline: one-by-one chaining, readiness gates, crash-restart, tab/content handling), MultiplerunRunConfiguration (persistence: readExternal/writeExternal, presets, env profiles) and MultiplerunMonitorPanel (the monitor tool window: table model, columns, batch actions, env switching) from Java to Kotlin. Public surfaces and behavior are unchanged - every getter/setter keeps its exact Java name. Only the GUI-form-bound run-config editor stays Java (its .form is tied to a Java class; migrating it means rewriting the UI in Kotlin UI DSL, deferred). No functional change.

2.0.6:

  • Internal (Kotlin migration, five classes): converted EnvVarsDialog (the read-only loaded-variables viewer), MultiplerunProcessRegistry (the per-project registry of running apps the monitor lists), MultiplerunStatusBarWidget, MemoryLimitWatcher (the background memory/health/CPU alert watcher) and MemoryChartDialog (the full-session memory chart + leak analysis + CSV export) from Java to Kotlin. Public surfaces and behavior are unchanged. No functional change.

2.0.5:

  • Internal (Kotlin migration, five classes): converted the IDE-glue registration classes - MultiplerunConfigurationType, ShowMultiplerunMonitorAction, MultiplerunMonitorToolWindowFactory, MultiplerunStatusBarWidgetFactory and StopRunningMultiplerunConfigurationsAction (the stop-all action and the per-project process registry it keeps) - from Java to Kotlin. Same class names/ids, so the plugin.xml registrations and every caller are untouched. No functional change.

2.0.4:

  • Internal (Kotlin migration, two classes): converted RunConfigurationHelper (env file parsing/merging, the "Ready when" condition parser, the env-override reflection fallbacks) and ProcessStatsSampler (ps/lsof/proc parsing, docker-stats-style formatting) from Java to Kotlin. Both public surfaces are unchanged, so every caller (the launch pipeline, the monitor, the status bar widget, the memory chart) keeps working exactly as before. No functional change.

2.0.3:

  • Internal (Kotlin migration): converted the docker-compose parser (ComposeImporter - reads mem_limit, env_file, depends_on, ports and topologically orders services) from Java to Kotlin. Its public surface is unchanged, so the run-config editor's "Import from docker-compose.yml" keeps working exactly as before. No functional change.

2.0.2:

  • Internal (Kotlin migration): converted the memory-history/leak-analysis helper (MemoryHistory, with its Sample/Analysis/trend model and CSV export) from Java to Kotlin. Its public surface is unchanged, so the monitor and the memory chart keep working exactly as before. No functional change.

2.0.1:

  • Maintenance (Marketplace verifier): migrated off the deprecated ProgramRunner.execute(environment, callback) - the environment is now built with its callback via ExecutionEnvironmentBuilder and run with the non-deprecated execute(environment). This clears the only deprecated-API warning on 2023.3–2024.x (those now verify with 0 warnings). No functional change.

2.0.0:

  • Internal milestone: started the incremental migration to Kotlin (hence the 2.0 bump). The build now compiles Java and Kotlin together (Kotlin stdlib provided by the IDE, not bundled); the first pure-logic class (the Logs filter) is now Kotlin. No user-facing change; the complex UI/launch classes stay Java for now and move over gradually.

1.45.3:

  • Maintenance (Marketplace verifier): removed the only internal-API usage - the runner now extends GenericProgramRunner, so the platform performs the ExecutionManager.startRunProfile call itself. No functional change.
  • Also migrated off three deprecated APIs (URL(String) → URI.toURL(), DefaultActionGroup.addAll(ActionGroup), FileChooserDescriptorFactory.createSingleFileDescriptor()). Verifier now reports 0 internal / 3 deprecated (down from 1 internal / 6-7 deprecated).

1.45.2:

  • Fix: after switching an app's environment, the monitor's Env column now shows the env actually in effect for that app (its per-app override), instead of still showing the group's profile.
  • The Switch Environment modal marks and pre-selects the active environment; the group-wide switch is authoritative - it clears the running apps' per-app overrides so they all follow the chosen environment (and the Env column shows it uniformly).

1.45.1:

  • Env switching (refines 1.45.0 after feedback): the Env column dropdown now switches just that application (a per-app override) and restarts only it - the toolbar Switch Environment button stays the group-wide "switch all" option.
  • Both now keep each app's executor: an app running under Debug comes back under Debug (Run stays Run, …). They relaunch the app through the group, so it stays tracked and shows its new environment.
  • The Switch Environment toolbar icon is now an environment-like icon (was a reddish one).

1.45.0:

  • Environment file: the group's env-file browse button now takes several .env files at once (Ctrl/Shift-select), instead of one per click, when building the profile list.
  • Monitor: when a group has more than one env profile, the Env column becomes a dropdown to switch the environment; a "view loaded variables" entry still opens the viewer.
  • Monitor: new Switch Environment toolbar button (badge = running apps) switches the environment of the running apps from a single modal, instead of app by app.
  • Tests: +6 unit tests (multi-file selection, switchable profiles, batch grouping). 145 total.

1.44.0:

  • Monitor: selecting several applications and then running a batch action (Restart / Stop / Force Kill) now keeps the whole selection across the automatic refresh - the action targets every selected app, no longer collapsing to a single row.
  • Monitor: new Restart All toolbar button with a badge showing the number of running applications - relaunches the whole set in one click, next to Stop All.
  • Tests: +3 unit tests for the multi-selection restore, 139 total.

1.43.0:

  • Build: migrated to the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin 2.x (the tooling JetBrains recommends) on Gradle 9. Same compatibility targets (2023.3+, no upper bound); no functional change to the plugin.
  • Build: the JetBrains Plugin Verifier now runs locally against the same IDE matrix the Marketplace verifies (2023.3.8 → 2026.1.4), so API problems are caught before publishing.
  • Tests: +6 unit tests (executor matching and alert-threshold clamps), 136 total.

1.42.2:

  • Maintenance: migrate off two platform APIs the Marketplace verifier flagged - the docker-compose import button no longer uses the removal-scheduled ToolbarDecorator.addExtraAction(AnActionButton), and child processes are launched via the public ProgramRunner.execute(env, callback) instead of the internal ExecutionEnvironment.setCallback. No functional change.

1.42.1:

  • Fix: Logs tab layout - the filter controls now sit as a full-width strip on top and the log fills the whole width below them (they were laid out as a left-hand column, pushing the log to the right).

1.42.0:

  • Logs tab: console output is now readable when apps emit ANSI color codes. By default the escape codes are stripped (clean text); tick ANSI in the header to render the real colors instead. Filtering always works on the clean text.
  • Build: keep a rolling archive of the last 5 built plugin zips in dist/ (which survives gradlew clean), so recent artifacts are never lost. No functional change to the plugin.

1.41.0:

  • Logs tab: an App selector shows the logs of a single application (or all), and advanced, composable filters - several comma-separated terms combined with any/all, matched as substring or regex, case-sensitive or not, to show or hide matches, plus a minimum log level (Info+/Warn+/ Errors) detected from the text.
  • Monitor: the Stop Multiple Run count now includes apps restarted individually from the monitor (which the IDE relaunches as standalone runs) - it no longer under-counts, and the button stops them too.

1.40.0:

  • Monitor: the memory Analysis tab now loads its per-process breakdown correctly (it was stuck on "Sampling…" inside the modal), and got richer leak analysis - a steady-leak verdict backed by the growth rate, projected growth per hour, R² of the trend and how often memory was never freed.
  • Monitor: the Analysis tab gained a process filter (by PID or command) and an Export analysis… button that saves the verdict plus the per-process breakdown as a text report.
  • Monitor: a new toolbar button opens the memory chart straight on the Analysis tab for the selected application - no need to click the Mem trend sparkline.
  • Monitor: the Stop Multiple Run toolbar button now shows the number of running processes next to a stop icon (like WebStorm), instead of a bare icon that was easy to confuse with the per-row Stop.

1.39.0:

  • Monitor: the memory chart (click a "Mem trend" sparkline) now has labeled X and Y axes - X is elapsed time, Y is memory (RSS) - with grid lines and tick labels.
  • Monitor: the memory chart gained an Analysis tab with a memory-trend / possible leak verdict (growing/stable/shrinking, with the growth rate) and a per-process breakdown of the application's process tree, so a runaway child process is easy to spot.
  • Monitor: show/hide columns - a toolbar button opens a checkbox list to choose which columns are visible.
  • Monitor: the Stop Multiple Run toolbar button now has a visible icon (it was blank because of a stale icon path).

1.38.0:

  • Monitor: click the Env cell of a running application to open a viewer with the environment variables Multiple Run loaded for it at launch (group variables, group env file, memory-limit options and per-app env file, merged). A filter at the top narrows by variable name, and values can be masked for screen sharing.
  • Monitor: the Status column now shows running for every live application (green), refining to healthy/down when a port/http "Ready when" condition is set - it no longer stays blank.

1.37.1:

  • Build: disable buildSearchableOptions - the plugin has no Settings pages to index, and that step launched a headless IDE that intermittently failed with a platform ConcurrentModificationException. No functional change.

1.37.0:

  • New: sustained CPU alert. Set a "CPU alert %" on the group and an application whose CPU stays at or above it for three consecutive background checks raises a notification (with a Restart button); the alert re-arms when it drops back. 0 disables it; values above 100 make sense on multi-core machines. Cross-platform.

1.36.0:

  • Monitor: batch actions. Select several rows (Ctrl/Shift-click) and Restart, Stop or Force Kill acts on all of them. New "Restart Unhealthy" toolbar action restarts every application whose port/http readiness check is currently down.

1.35.0:

  • Monitor: click the "Mem trend" sparkline of a row to open a full-session memory chart for that application (the sparkline only shows the last minute). The chart pop-up can export the history to CSV (timestamp, RSS, percent).

1.34.0:

  • New: crash and health alerts with a one-click Restart. When an app crashes and "Restart on crash" is off (or its attempts are used up), a notification now offers a Restart button instead of failing silently. And an app whose port:/ http "Ready when" condition stays down for three consecutive background checks is reported unhealthy, also with a Restart button; the alert re-arms when the app recovers.

1.33.0:

  • New: status bar widget. A compact indicator shows how many applications Multiple Run is running, their combined memory and how many are unhealthy (a port/http "Ready when" that is currently down). Click it to open the Multiple Run Monitor. Toggle it from the status bar widgets menu.

1.32.0:

  • New: per-application environment file. The applications table has an "Env file (app)" column - point an app at its own .env file and it overrides the group's environment (variables and env file) just for that app. Empty = use the group's environment. Re-read on every run; relative paths resolve against the project root.

1.31.0:

  • Monitor: the Ports column is now clickable - click a port to open http://localhost:<port> in the browser (a menu lets you pick when a process listens on several ports). Ports render as links.

1.30.0:

  • New: import from docker-compose.yml. The editor's list toolbar gains an import button that reads a compose file and applies it to the run configurations whose name matches a service: mem_limit (and deploy.resources.limits.memory) becomes the Memory limit, env_file becomes an environment profile, and depends_on reorders the list (dependencies first) and adds a port: "Ready when" gate. Services without a matching run configuration are reported and skipped.

1.29.0:

  • New: execution presets. Save the current On/Off selection of applications plus the active environment profile as a named preset, and switch between scenarios ("backend only", "full stack", ...) from a dropdown in the editor - no more re-checking boxes by hand.

1.28.1:

  • Fix: the run configuration editor (Edit Configurations for a Multiple Run entry) could fail to open after the 1.27.2 package rename - the GUI form bound to the editor was accidentally removed. Restored it.

1.28.0:

  • New: the Multiple Run Monitor tool window has a second "Logs" tab - an aggregated view of the console output of every running application, like docker compose logs -f. Each line is prefixed with its application name in a distinct color, and a filter field narrows the view to matching lines. The old table is now the "Processes" tab.

1.27.2:

  • Internal: renamed the Java package from the original author's namespace to io.github.welingtonmonteiro.multiplerun. No user-facing change - existing run configurations keep working (the "Multirun" configuration type id is unchanged).

1.27.1:

  • Fix: the "Memory limit (MB)" and "Ready when" cells no longer lose focus while typing (the cell editor was being closed by the dialog's validation cycle).

1.27:

  • Monitor: now lists EVERY process the IDE is running - standalone (singleton) runs included, not only the ones started by Multiple Run. The Name column shows the origin: the Multiple Run icon for grouped apps, the run configuration's own icon (node, npm, jest, ...) for standalone ones.
  • Monitor: an application restarted from the monitor no longer disappears from the list, and keeps showing its group, env profile and memory limit.
  • Monitor: columns are resizable - drag the header edges to adjust widths.

1.26:

  • Monitor: new "Mem trend" sparkline column - a mini chart with the memory history of the last minute per application (green/orange/red by how close to the limit it is), so leaks and growth trends are visible at a glance.
  • Windows support for the monitor: memory and CPU are sampled through PowerShell Get-Process when ps is not available. (Ports and kill-by-port still need lsof, i.e. Linux/macOS.)

1.25:

  • New: restart policies, docker style. "Restart application on crash" relaunches an app that exits with a crash code (max 3 attempts per run); stops via the stop buttons never trigger it. The memory limit alert threshold is now configurable (default 90%) and the action can be "Notify" or "Restart application" - docker-like OOM handling.

1.24:

  • New: enable/disable checkbox per application - unchecked apps stay in the list but are not launched. Great for temporarily skipping a service without losing its settings.
  • New: "Ready when" column, a docker-compose-like readiness gate for one-by-one starts. The next application only starts when the previous one is ready: port:3003 (TCP port open), an http(s) health URL (2xx/3xx) or log:some text (console output contains it). Capped at 2 minutes, then the chain continues anyway.
  • Monitor: new "Status" column - apps with a port/http readiness condition are re-checked on every refresh and show healthy/down, like docker ps.
  • Monitor: double click on a row jumps to the console tab of that application.

1.23:

  • New: environment profiles. The Environment file field is now an editable dropdown that remembers every .env file you use - switch between environments (for example .env.development, .env.staging, .env.production) by picking a profile, no more retyping paths. The monitor shows the active profile of each running application in the new "Env" column.

1.22.1:

  • Monitor: the selected row is no longer deselected by the automatic refresh.
  • Monitor: fix CPU % stuck at 0.00% on Linux - the ps TIME column only has 1-second resolution, so the sampler now reads /proc/[pid]/stat (10 ms ticks) instead.

1.22:

  • Multiple Run Monitor: Restart action per row - stop and start again only the selected application, the rest of the group keeps running.
  • Multiple Run Monitor: CPU % is now instantaneous (delta between two samples, like docker stats) instead of the average since the process started.
  • New: memory limit alert. When an application with a configured memory limit crosses 90% of it, the IDE shows a warning notification - even with the monitor closed. One alert per process.
  • Multiple Run Monitor: new "Uptime" column.

1.21:

  • Multiple Run Monitor: new "Ports" column showing the TCP ports each application is listening on (like the PORTS column of docker ps).
  • Multiple Run Monitor: Stop and Force Kill actions per row (toolbar and right-click) - Force Kill sends SIGKILL to the whole process tree of the selected application.
  • Multiple Run Monitor: "Kill Process on Port" action - type a TCP port and kill whatever process is listening on it (with confirmation), even processes not started by the plugin. Goodbye EADDRINUSE.

1.20:

  • New: "Multiple Run Monitor" tool window (bottom stripe, also under Run -> Multiple Run Monitor). A docker-stats-like live table with every application started by Multiple Run: PID, memory usage vs. the configured limit (or the machine total), memory percentage and CPU. Measures the whole process tree of each application (npm wrapper + node child, etc.) and refreshes automatically every 2 seconds.

1.19:

  • New: per-application memory limit. The configurations list is now a table with an editable "Memory limit (MB)" column - type a heap cap right next to each application and it is applied at launch as NODE_OPTIONS --max-old-space-size (Node.js) and JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS -Xmx (JVM), the process-level analog of docker's mem_limit.

1.18:

  • New: Save console logs option. Point the configuration to a folder and the console output of every configuration in the list is also written there as <name>.log, using the IDE's standard "save console output to file" mechanism. Relative paths resolve against the project root.

1.17:

  • New: Environment file option. Point the Multiple Run configuration to a .env file (browse button or type the path; relative paths resolve against the project root) and its KEY=VALUE entries are applied to every configuration in the list. The file is re-read on every run; variables configured manually in the Environment variables field win over the file on conflicts.
  • Environment override now also reaches npm/pnpm/yarn run configurations.
  • Diagnostics: idea.log records which injection strategy each grouped configuration took (variable names only, never values).

1.16.2:

  • Migrate off deprecated platform APIs flagged by the Marketplace verifier (RunnerRegistry.getRunner, ProcessAdapter, ListCellRendererWrapper), keeping the plugin compatible with future IDE versions. No functional changes.

1.16.1:

  • Use an own id for the "Stop Multiple Run" action, fixing the "ID is already taken" PluginException on startup when the original Multirun plugin is installed alongside. Note: the two plugins still cannot run together (they share the run configuration type) - uninstall the original Multirun.

1.16:

  • New: restart behavior, like the built-in Compound configuration. Running a Multirun that is already running now stops the processes it started before (waiting for their termination) and then starts again - no need to use "Stop Multirun" first. Enabled by default; can be disabled per configuration with the new "Restart running configurations before starting" option. Only the processes of the restarted Multirun are stopped - other running Multirun groups are not affected.
  • The run configuration type is now shown as "Multiple Run" in the Add New Configuration list (the internal type id is unchanged, existing configurations keep working). The stop action is now "Stop Multiple Run".

1.15.2:

  • Reference grouped run configurations by their configuration type id instead of the display name. Fixes matching with plugins whose type display name differs (e.g. BashSupport Pro's Shell-compatible configurations) and with translated IDEs (language packs). Existing configurations keep working and are migrated automatically on the next save.

1.15.1:

  • Fix delay value corruption in locales that use a comma as the decimal separator (German, pt-BR, ...): the field now accepts both "." and "," and persisted values are no longer misread as tens (e.g. "-1.0" turning into -10).

1.15:

  • New: Environment variables option on the Multirun configuration. The variables are applied to every configuration in the list (overriding same-named variables), including nested Multirun configurations. The "Include system environment variables" flag is applied to children as well.

1.14.2:

  • Fix cycle detection when a Multirun contains multiple nested Multirun configurations.
  • Fix delay value being reset to 0 in locales that use a comma as the decimal separator.
  • Run tab updates (icon/name/pin) now happen on the EDT to avoid "must be called on EDT" errors.
  • Build against IntelliJ Platform 2023.3 with Gradle 8.5; drop internal *Impl API usage and other cleanups.

1.14.1:

  • Parsing the delay with respect to current locale.
  • Add profiler run configurations support.

1.14:

  • Add support for 2023.3 version of IntelliJ based IDEs.
  • Fix "must be called on EDT exception"
  • Disable delay input if "Start configuration one by one" is disabled

1.13:

  • Add support for 2021.2 version of IntelliJ based IDEs.

1.12:

  • Stop using some of deprecated IntelliJ Platform API.
  • Move to Plugin SDK using Java 11.

  • Add plugin log icon.

1.11:

  • Add support for sub-second delay.
  • Fix waiting for delay when no more configurations to run.
  • Add support for Coverage executor.
  • Enable re-using tabs with successful and failure results.
  • Fix issue when tabs couldn't be re-used after 'Stop Multirun' command.
  • Support serial execution of the configurations (Use 'Start configurations one by one' and use negative delay)
  • When 'Start configurations one by one' used with delay, do not wait till delay to start next configuration.

action.description: Show memory and CPU usage of the applications started by Multiple Run
